diagnose.title: Diagnostics
diagnose.subtitle: Find out why a window does not stay where you place it.
diagnose.keep: Leave the window placed when done
diagnose.warning: This really moves the window for a few seconds.
diagnose.empty.title: Pick a window and press Diagnose
diagnose.empty.body: We will watch the window for a few seconds and tell you which game setting would help.
diagnose.no_reaction: The window did not react: no changes observed
diagnose.legend: t (ms since the first write) · ▲ our write · ● window change · | revert latency
diagnose.chart_hint: Hover a mark, or focus the chart and use ← → (+ and - to zoom).
diagnose.table.title: Timeline data
diagnose.verdict.accepted.headline: The window accepted the change and stays where we placed it
diagnose.verdict.style_reverted.headline: The game fights back: it restores the frame we removed
diagnose.verdict.size_forced.headline: The game imposes its own window size
diagnose.verdict.position_forced.headlin: The game moves the window back after it is moved
diagnose.verdict.style_and_size_reverted: The game fights back: it reverts the frame and its size
diagnose.verdict.late_revert.headline: The game waits and reverts the changes later
diagnose.tip.head: t = {t} · {origin}
diagnose.rec.style_reverted: {process} restores the window frame after it is removed. Check that its settings do not force framed windowed mode; Borderless Shatter re-asserts the style up to {max_reasserts} times per cycle and stops insisting if the game fights back.
diagnose.rec.position_forced: {process} moves the window back after it is moved, although it keeps the size. Look for a game option that locks or centres the window position.
diagnose.rec.warscape_resolution: Warscape engine: with the game closed and after backing up preferences.script.txt, set fix_res false, fix_window_pos false, x_res {x_res} and y_res {y_res} ({how}).
diagnose.rec.warscape_how_unaware: the game is DPI-unaware: use the island size ({w}x{h}) divided by dpi/96 (this monitor is at {pct}, dpi {dpi}: {x_res}x{y_res})
diagnose.rec.unity_args: Unity engine: launch the game with -popupwindow -screen-width {width} -screen-height {height} (the island size; Unity asks for a supported resolution, if it does not honour it try another).
diagnose.rec.game_resolution: If you cannot change the game, add game_resolution {"width": {width}, "height": {height}} to its profile: the window will be centred in the island at that size instead of fighting.
